name: the_same_code_embossed
why: The same inscription, at the same height, in the same place, EMBOSSED instead of engraved: the volume must go the other way, by the SAME number. It is the pair that says the operation knows which direction it is working in -- an extrusion that grows into the part, or a cut that goes outwards, gives no error: it gives a volume that does not change, and nobody looks at the volume.
_why_the_same_number: 230.70 mm3 removed and 230.70 added are not two measurements: they are the same measurement with two signs, and the fact that they coincide says that the area of the letters does not depend on what is done with it. On a 3D print the relief is what is really used -- a cavity of half a millimetre is not made by the nozzle.

expect.tolerance_why: it is the same volume as the engraving, with the same tessellation noise

expect.why: the same ratio as the engraving: the letters are the same, what changes is which way the material goes
the relief must JOIN the part. If it stayed detached the bodies would be two, the feature would be green just the same, and five loose letters would arrive at the workshop.

expect.tolerance_why: it is the starting volume plus that of the letters, with the same noise
expect.why: THE VOLUME WENT UP. In the engraved case the same step made it go down by as much: it is the line that tells «raised» from an argument that is copied into the answer and ignored.

THE PART HAS BECOME THICKER BY EXACTLY THE 2 mm OF THE RELIEF. The volume alone would not say which way the letters grew: a relief that grew inwards would add zero, but a relief that grows the right way shows here and only here.
